intro: Key frames from the film, as the player sees them: the phone's screen at the game's own size (two picture pixels to a game pixel), the stone, the Warrior, the camera following him to the end where the Colossus comes up; then closer, at twice. His shovel, beat by beat: he sinks; the tell, held over a second, the water boiling off one end; he bursts up there, his maw turned on its side, gaping across the stone; his tentacles scrape along the stone toward his mouth, one along each edge in turn, the Warrior weaving through the gaps; a hit knocks him toward the mouth; too close and the jaws snap shut; then he goes back to his place.
blocks: Frames from his stand (30 a second). He sinks out of his stand in 0.73 s, his tentacles with him, the last of him his eye's fire fading into the deep; then the tell, held 1.13 s: the water boiling and heaving off the end he will come up at, the camera following the Warrior there.
THE TELL, held: the left end boiling
HE BURSTS UP AT THE END; THE ROAR

The strike: four frames, smeared, the screen jolted; his maw on its side, one jaw along each edge of the stone, gaping across its whole depth; water pouring off him; the roar; then his gape, his tongue-eye weaving, never still.
THE SHOVEL: THE TENTACLES SCRAPE ALONG THE STONE; THE HIT

One along each edge in turn, out of the water past the far end, scraping to his maw at 12 tiles a second, sparks, grit and slime thrown back, the stone scored: the back edge's tip hooked down, its gap at the near edge; the near edge's curled up, its gap at the back. The Warrior weaves low, then high, and is caught at the edge of a gap and knocked toward the mouth.
the Warrior low, in its gap
HIT: caught by its curled tip
down by his maw; tentacle 2 at it

The Warrior too close: the twitch, held (his jaws flexing wider, his tongue-eye drawn in) as he gets up and leaps away; the strike, two smeared frames, lunging up out of the water and leaning out over the stone's end, slamming shut; held shut, spittle and spray bursting; back, gaping again.
THE LAST TWO; DRAWN BACK; HE GOES BACK
Each tentacle drawn back off the stone into the water at his maw and slid back under; tentacles 3 and 4; then he sinks at the end and comes up at his place, a short rise, into his stand.
tentacle 3 drawn back into the water
up at his place, into his stand
Each end painted, not mirrored (each turned its own way round, as the camera sees it there): the same shovel at the right end, the Warrior weaving through all four.
